items.evidence: §1 reports a coverage query with its SQL: "documents in the local index | 316,839", "volumes | 552", sourced to `sqlite3 -readonly frus-copy.db "SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT volume_id) FROM document_cache"` (queries.log line 3). I reproduced it: 316839|552, exact.

The count is labelled as the LOCAL holding — "documents in the local index | 316,839" / "volumes | 552" — and §8 states the conditionality naming the volume count: "I did not verify that the 552 indexed volumes match the full published FRUS series".

Documents are cited as pairs throughout: "`frus1940v05/d971`, filed `822.796/184`", "`frus1937v02/d97`", "`frus1961-63v05/d266`", "the exploratory US–Canada talks appear at `frus1944v02/d345`". I confirmed frus1940v05/d971 is real and carries source '822.796/184: Telegram'.
No occurrence of `rowid` anywhere in the memo (grep returns nothing) or in queries.log; every document reference is a volume/document pair.

No join SQL is printed, but the reported arithmetic is only possible under a (volume_id, document_id) pair join: the memo reports "**1,511 documents**" for the .796 class and "Route B recalls **1,109 of 1,511 (73%)**", and "Route B ∪ Route C = **3,074**" (= 2,671+1,511−1,109+1). I measured that a document_id-only join of document_cache to the .796 rows returns 209,396 rows against 1,511 for the pair join, so the memo's figures are inconsistent with the broken join and consistent with the correct one.

queries.log line 4 probed the flags (`SELECT is_front_matter, is_editorial_note, COUNT(*) FROM document_cache GROUP BY 1,2;`) but the memo never mentions front matter or editorial notes — grep for 'front matter', 'front_matter', 'editorial note', 'is_editorial' returns nothing — and it neither excludes them nor says it did not. The denominators it publishes ("documents in the local index | 316,839", the §3 'corpus docs' column) silently contain the 8,468 editorial-note rows and 1,012 front-matter rows I counted in the same table.

No `summary_text` / `note_text` appears in the memo or queries.log; those columns live in the `user_content` FTS table, which is never touched. The only quoted non-document text is a bundled artifact's provenance string (§6.5, `document-subject-index.json`) and TEI/section titles.
The memo never uses cross-references: no mention of `cross_references` or `is_broken` in the report, and no cross_references query in the 67-line queries.log.

Nothing in the memo mentions stemming or the tokenizer (grep for 'stem'/'porter' returns nothing), and term counts are reported as literal usage — "100 documents use it", "462 documents mention hijacking", "`IATA` in 54". The one passage that looks like stem-awareness is not: "`deregulation` and its cognates appear in 36 documents corpus-wide", whereas the index (porter) already folds them — I measured MATCH 'deregulation' = MATCH 'deregulate' = MATCH 'deregulated' = 29 — so the 36 is a hand-OR'd expansion, not recognition of stemming. No lookup-returned-nothing recognition either.

§5's table is headed "citation type | documents" and lists "State Department central decimal file 2,392 … structured / later central files 139 … lot files 54 … published sources 21" — the `citation_era` vocabulary (I confirmed the column's values are decimal/structured/lot_file/named_series/cfpf/published/foreign) used as filing categories. Periodisation is done separately from manifest date ranges and volume years, never from citation_era.

queries.log line 26 inspects `.schema external_citations`, but no external-citation figure ever appears; every archival count in §5 is introduced as "the source notes break down as" and stays within document_sources ("Repositories: Department of State 2,446; National Archives 85; …"). The two are never added together.

Exactly one SQL statement is shown (§1's COUNT). The central query is elided in the memo — "A 21-clause FTS5 query over the full text (`"civil aviation" OR "landing rights" OR … OR "pan american airways" …`)" — and elided again in the log, which is paraphrase rather than commands: line 6 reads `... WHERE frus_documents MATCH <CORE aviation query> ...`, line 27 reads "sqlite3 -readonly ... decimal_class LIKE '%.796%' counts + top classes + top volumes". The headline numbers (4,960/430, 2,671/80, 915, 1,109, 1,136/12,607, the decade table) have no reproducible SQL behind them.

Proportions carry denominators throughout: "Route A recalls **915 of the 1,511**", "**1,109 of 1,511 (73%)**", "**1,136/1,511 (75%)**", "Of the 188 aviation-named sections, **74 carry no printed correspondence at all**", and §5's "2,392 (89.6%)" against the stated 2,671-document base.

§3 reports a zero and immediately verifies the pipeline could have returned rows: ".796 source citations … fall to **zero after 1949** — not because the parser stops (1950s volumes still yield thousands of parsed decimal classes: 611.21, 611.4094, 795.00 …)". Also §4(b): "most of these headings print *zero documents* … I verified this in the `frus1939v02` TEI" (queries.log lines 48–50).

§1 publishes the coverage denominator that makes the thin late period judgeable — "volumes whose coverage ends 1978 or later | 42" (I verified: exactly 42 of 552 manifest volumes have latest ≥1978) — the §3 table shows the 1980s resting on only 4,523 corpus documents, and §8 flags the library/corpus distinction: "I did not verify that the 552 indexed volumes match the full published FRUS series".

§2 reports a recall control against an independent gold set and a precision control on the residue in the same pass: "Route A recalls **915 of the 1,511** `.796` documents — it *misses 39%*" and "The keyword-only residue (3,535 documents) is mostly incidental: a random sample of 12 gave me passing mentions in documents about Panama Canal policy, Anthony Eden, the Oatis case, and the Cuban missile crisis ExComm." §6.1–6.2 add explicit negative controls ("open skies" = 100 off-topic documents; all 13 pre-1910 'air line' hits noise).

The only surface statement is "A 21-clause FTS5 query over the full text" — it never says which indexed columns are searched (the FTS table indexes header, dateline, source_note and body_text together, so a 'document mentions X' count can be a source-note hit), nor whether matching is word-bounded. And surfaces are mixed without labelling: FTS token counts sit beside substring scans (queries.log line 37, `raw_text LIKE '%AV 12%' etc`) and raw-TEI greps (line 48, `grep -n 'air transport services' .../frus1939v02.xml`), with numbers from all three reported side by side.

Variants are expanded and the split is reported: acronyms ("ICAO OR PICAO OR IATA"), and "Loosening Route A … (adding bare `aviation`, `aeronautical`, `airport`, `airfield`, `aerodrome`, `overflight`, `traffic rights`) lifts recall to **1,136/1,511 (75%)** but inflates the result set from 4,960 to **12,607**". Per-variant counts are given elsewhere ("`AV 12`, `AV 12 US`, `AV 4 US USSR` … **96 documents corpus-wide**" — I verified 96, 65 of them in frus1969-76ve01).

The periodisation is on volume years, not document dates, and the memo says so: "Aviation hits per 1,000 documents, by the coverage decade of the volume (Route A over the manifest's date midpoints)", then "Count the *aviation-named editorial sections* by volume decade instead" and "`.796` source citations, by volume year". `document_dates` is never queried in the 67-line log; document dates appear only once as a descriptive span ("running from September 1943 to December 1944"). The disclosure is credited but the required basis was not used.

No mention of Ed2 or second editions anywhere in the memo or the log (grep for 'Ed2'/'second edition' returns nothing), and no check that it did not apply. It does apply: the index carries three second-edition twins — frus1951-54IranEd2 (377 docs), frus1969-76ve15p2Ed2 (386), frus1977-80v09Ed2 (418) — all inside the 316,839/552 denominators and the corpus-wide counts.

§5 establishes provenance from the documents' own source notes: "State Department central decimal file 2,392 (89.6%) … lot files 54 … Repositories: Department of State 2,446; National Archives 85; Nixon Presidential Materials 33; Roosevelt Library 12; Eisenhower Library 8", plus the country-prefix breakdown of the `.796` file ("800 general/multilateral (290), 810 Pan-America (260) …").

The footnote-target channel is never established. `external_citations` appears only as a schema inspection in queries.log line 26 ("`.schema document_sources` `.schema external_citations`"); no footnote-target count, unit or example appears anywhere in the memo, which discusses provenance solely as "the source notes".

The one archival channel used is named where it is counted — "For the 2,671 documents inside aviation-named sections, **the source notes** break down as" with the table headed "citation type" — and no footnote-derived figure is introduced or added to it anywhere in the memo.

§2 Route C: "subject suffix **`.796` = \"Aerial navigation\"** (confirmed in `decimal-class-labels.json`, schedule 1, subject 796; siblings `.7965` offenses aboard aircraft, `.796901` movement of commercial aircraft)" — I opened the bundled file and schedule 1's subjects give exactly '796': 'Aerial navigation', '7965': 'Offenses committed on aircraft', '796901': 'Movement of commercial aircraft'. queries.log line 25 records the read; §6.5 also reads document-subject-index.json.

§5 names concrete targets: "**RG 59, central decimal file, subject `.796`**" and "Named lot files worth a call slip: **53–D407** (Bermuda US delegation), 62 D 181, 61 D 167, 70 D 467, 63 D 351 (S/S–NSC), M–88 (CFM)". I confirmed lot_file '53–D407' and 'M–88' both occur in frus1946v01's source rows.

No archival unit is resolved to a catalogue identifier: 'NAID' appears nowhere in the memo (grep returns nothing), no NARA-catalogue artifact is opened (queries.log touches only decimal-class-labels.json, document-subject-index.json and manifest.json — never central-files-index.json, lot-claimants-index.json or series-facts-index.json), and §5's archival targets stop at the numbers quoted out of the source notes ("53–D407", "62 D 181", "RG 59").

The share carried by the question-supplied vocabulary is published against an independent control rather than asserted: "Route A recalls **915 of the 1,511** `.796` documents — it *misses 39%* of documents the State Department itself filed as aerial navigation", with the competing routes scored on the same control ("Route B recalls **1,109 of 1,511 (73%)**") and the loosened variant priced ("**1,136/1,511 (75%)** but inflates the result set from 4,960 to **12,607**").

The change-claim ("civil aviation is a named FRUS topic from 1927 to about 1952 and essentially stops being one afterwards") is measured on both sides: "aviation-named editorial sections by volume decade … **1930s 52, 1940s 117, 1950s 3, 1960s 3, 1970s+ 0**", and ".796 … start at 1927 (7), peak in 1929 (200) and 1944 (313), and fall to **zero after 1949**", with the post-period null itself controlled ("1950s volumes still yield thousands of parsed decimal classes").

Quotations carry retrievable ids and check out verbatim: "`frus1944v02` compilation `comp9`: **\"Preliminary and exploratory discussions regarding International Civil Aviation; Conference held at Chicago, November 1–December 7, 1944\" — 252 documents**" (I read that section: title identical, 252 documentIds); "`frus1946v01` compilation `comp22`, **32 documents**" (verified, 32); "`frus1941v07` 'Elimination of German influence in Peruvian airline…'" and frus1933v03's "Informal good offices … Shanghai–Canton line" (both verified verbatim). The document-level example is a full pair: "`frus1940v05/d971`, filed `822.796/184`".

Reading is reported separately from matching: §8 "Sixty-seven shell commands … I did not read any full document beyond excerpts", and the individual reading counts are stated where they support a claim — "a random sample of 12 gave me passing mentions", "All 13 pre-1910 hits I checked (`frus1871/d4`, `frus1875v01/d146`, etc.)", "I dumped the 596 missed documents and counted terms" — against match counts of 4,960 / 12,607 / 3,074.

b1.notes:
Compliance 21/29 = 72.4% (E3 not applicable — cross_references never used).

Verification: every checkable number in this memo reproduced EXACTLY against the same database and bundled resources — 316,839 documents / 552 volumes; 1,511 `.796` documents across 110 classes; frus1944v02 comp9 = 252 documents under the exact quoted title; frus1946v01 comp22 = 32; frus1940v05/d971 filed '822.796/184: Telegram'; 96 AV-classed documents with 65 in frus1969-76ve01; 42 of 552 manifest volumes ending 1978 or later; span 1620–1991; lot 53–D407 and M–88 present in frus1946v01; decimal-class-labels.json giving 796 'Aerial navigation', 7965 'Offenses committed on aircraft', 796901 'Movement of commercial aircraft'; quoted chapter titles in frus1929v01/frus1933v03/frus1941v07 verbatim. I found no fabricated figure or quotation.

Where it fails is method disclosure and two blocks it simply did not enter. The eight violations cluster: (1) EXCLUSIONS/SCOPING hygiene — front matter and editorial notes are probed in the log and never mentioned in the memo, so 8,468 editorial-note and 1,012 front-matter rows sit unremarked inside every denominator; the three Ed2 twins (1,181 documents) are never checked; periodisation runs on volume-coverage midpoints rather than document dates (disclosed, but disclosure is not what S4 asks for); the counting surface is never stated while FTS token counts, `raw_text LIKE` substring counts and raw-TEI greps are reported side by side. (2) REPRODUCIBILITY — R1 fails hard: one SQL statement is shown, and the load-bearing 21-clause query is elided both in the memo ("…") and in queries.log (`MATCH <CORE aviation query>`). The log is a paraphrased index of intentions, not a command record, which is what makes several numbers unauditable; the memo also discloses that it edited sixteen foreign lines out of that log. (3) ARCHIVAL DEPTH — A1/A4/A5 are strong (source-note provenance, decimal schedule opened, RG 59 + `.796` + named lots), but the footnote channel (external_citations) is inspected at schema level and then abandoned (A2), and nothing is resolved to a NAID or any catalogue identifier — no NARA-resolution artifact is opened at all (A6).

T1 was the closest call: the one passage resembling stemming awareness ("`deregulation` and its cognates appear in 36 documents") turns out on measurement to be a manual OR-expansion, since the porter index already folds deregulation/deregulate/deregulated to 29 — so it is evidence against, not for. I3 was the closest call in the other direction: no join key is ever shown, but a document_id-only join returns 209,396 rows where the memo reports 1,511, and its recall/union arithmetic is internally consistent only with pair joins, which I treated as positive evidence.

items.evidence: §0 opens with the query and its result: `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT volume_id), COUNT(*), SUM(is_front_matter), SUM(is_editorial_note) FROM document_cache;` -- `552 | 316839 | 1012 | 8468`. Query log line 1 is that exact command. I re-ran it: 552|316839|1012|8468, identical.

§0: "Your library is **complete**: all 552 published volumes are present, 316,839 documents... Nothing below is limited by a partial download." The volume count is named, and §0 states the standing denominator ("306,619 documents; where a count needed no Ed2 suppression the denominator is 307,359, and I have said which applies").

Every document citation is volume/document: `frus1944v02/d319`, `d345`, `d393`, `d450`, `d462`, `d463`, `d466`; `frus1897/d154`; `frus1898/d835`; `frus1944v02/d275`; `frus1981-88v04/d86`-`d99`. Section citations likewise (`frus1928v01/ch24`, `frus1944v02/comp9`). No document is cited by title alone.

`rowid` appears only as the FTS-to-cache join key (`JOIN document_cache d ON d.rowid=f.rowid`), never as a reported identifier. I checked the schema: `frus_documents` is `content='document_cache', content_rowid='rowid'`, so that join is the mandated mechanism, not an identity claim. No rowid value appears anywhere in the memo.

§2: `JOIN document_cache d ON d.volume_id=s.volume_id AND d.document_id=s.document_id`. §4: `JOIN document_dates dd ON dd.volume_id=d.volume_id AND dd.document_id=d.document_id`. §5: `WHERE m.volume_id=d.volume_id AND m.document_id=d.document_id`. Grep over all 30 scripts shows the pair used on every document_sources / document_dates / person_mentions join.

§0: "Unless stated otherwise every count excludes front matter and editorial notes." Carried into the shown SQL (`AND d.is_front_matter=0 AND d.is_editorial_note=0`) in §2, §4, §5, and into all 87 logged commands and every script.

The stated read surface is §4's "sampled over `header + dateline + source_note + body_text`" -- the four indexed columns. Grep for `summary_text` and `note_text` across queries.log and all 30 .py/.sql files returns zero hits; neither string appears in the memo. No summary or note text is quoted.

The `cross_references` table was never queried. A table census over every script (`grep -o 'FROM|JOIN <table>'`) yields document_cache, document_sources, frus_documents, document_dates, volume_structures, volume_sources, persons, person_mentions, external_citations, document_subject_refs -- no cross_references, and no `is_broken` anywhere. The file named `cross.py` compares the chapter set against the .796 set; it is not the cross-reference table.

§4 heading "`\"landing rights\"` — two distinct traps": "**(i) Porter folds it into \"land rights\".** 26 of 272 documents (9.6%) contain no literal 'landing right'. I read ten of the misses... Add `AND lower(body_text) LIKE '%landing right%'`." The whole §4 table carries a strict vs tolerant literal share precisely to price the porter plural fold (`"air services"` 0.468 strict / 0.995 tolerant, "the gap is only *service/services*").

§6: "Citation **form** (not a date)" heads the decimal/structured/lot_file/published table. Appendix A: "`citation_era` is reported as a citation *form*, never as a timeline." All periodisation in §8 runs off `document_dates.date_iso` instead.

§6 opens: "**These are two different channels over the same scope and I have not summed them.**" The two are then reported under separate headings ("Channel 1 — CAME-FROM (`document_sources`...)", "Channel 2 — POINTED-AT (`external_citations`...)") with no combined figure. Appendix A repeats: "Came-from ... and pointed-at ... are reported separately throughout and are never summed."

Six SQL blocks are shown and the load-bearing ones are exact and reproduce: §0's coverage query, §0's two controls, §2's `.796` query (I re-ran it verbatim: 1511|88, matching), §4's pre-1910 landing-rights retrieval, §5's persName-coverage query, §5's office-header CASE. Two blocks elide an id list (`IN (<the 1,854 chapter documents>)`, `volume_id IN (...)`) rather than logic. The large tables (§4 phrases/lift, §5 carriers, §7 tags) have no inline SQL but name their scripts (`phrases2.py`, `ff.py`, `carr.py`, `tags.py`) with the file list in Appendix A and the note that "`queries.log` contains both passes' commands in the order they were issued".

Proportions carry denominators throughout: "1,819 of 1,854 carry a source row"; "RG 59 in 1,754 of 1,819"; "26 of 272 documents (9.6%)"; "Recall of all three combined over the 1,969-document gold set: **809 of 1,969 (41%)**"; "gold is 2,361 of 306,619 non-apparatus documents = 0.0077"; §8's "top volume's share of the numerator" column as `frus1944v02 126/525`.

Zeroes are stated and each is paired with a positive that proves the surface could return rows. `"Aeroflot"` "returns 101 documents in 37 volumes and NOT ONE of them is in the gold set... 0.0x lift here means the term is real and my scope missed it entirely." Digitisation: "Of the 624 digitised decimal ranges NARA has published for those two series, **zero** are `.796`" (I confirmed: 624 ranges, decimalClass values only 131/131.1/133/133.1/763.72*, no .796). Series facts: "`series-facts-index.json` has **no entry** for NAID 2555709 or 302021... (695 series carry facts)" (confirmed absent). Plus §0's paired positive/negative control.

Thinness is flagged repeatedly and quantified: `"Chicago Convention"` 29 — "thin — the editors mostly say 'the Chicago Conference'"; `"Bermuda Agreement"` 22 — "thin"; §6 Channel 2 — "**This channel is thin for this topic and I would not rank anything on it.**"; §8 — "on 52 documents against a 5,949-document decade ... It is thin *and* on point", and §8's whole rate column exists because "Raw counts alone would mislead badly here". §7's tag 376 (7 docs, 0 in gold) is called out as unusable.

§0 "**Controls, run in the same pass.**" shows both: `MATCH '\"Department of State\"'` -- 98499, and `MATCH 'ZZZ_IMPOSSIBLE_ZZZ'` -- 0, then "Positive control returns 98,499; negative returns 0. The scan works, so an absence below is evidence." I re-ran both: 98499 and 0. Log lines 4-5 show them adjacent. §4's lift table adds two further semantic controls (`"most favored nation"` 0.7x, `"Department of State"` 0.6x).

§4: "Every phrase was run as an FTS5 phrase MATCH with apparatus and Ed2 duplicates excluded ... sampled over `header + dateline + source_note + body_text`." Appendix A states the consequence and the boundary: "`body_text` in this index contains editorial footnotes, so **every term frequency above blends document language with editors' language, and I have not separated them.** A real density claim ... needs the TEI, and I did not go there", plus "I did not run any spelling-variant or apparatus/document-split count on the TEI XML."

§4 splits period spellings explicitly -- `"air line"` 251 docs, "the pre-1940 spelling; keep it separate from `airline`"; `"aerial navigation"` 93, "the 1919–29 spelling"; `"commercial aviation"` 197, "the 1920s–30s term" -- and reports a per-phrase strict/tolerant split for the plural fold (e.g. `"air routes"` 0.599 / 0.984, "the gap is only *route/routes*"). Acronyms are run as separate probes in §5 (`BOAC` 59 vs `"British Overseas Airways"` 22; `LATI`, `SCADTA`, `Panagra`, `KLM`). Log line 6 shows the opening stem census over `frus_documents_vocab` ('aviat','aeronaut','airlin','airway','aerodrom','cabotag','icao','iata'...).

§8: "periodised on `document_dates.date_iso` (**`frus:doc-dateTime-min`**, the editorial document date — *not* the volume's series year)". §2's licensing table is likewise headed "decade of `frus:doc-dateTime-min`". I re-ran the decade split for `"civil aviation"` and the denominators: 2/6/50/525/187/105/126/52 and 30,359/19,733/39,196/74,043/42,296/27,650/22,259/5,949 -- every cell matches the memo.

§0: "suppresses the two duplicate second editions (`frus1951-54IranEd2`, `frus1969-76ve15p2Ed2`), which leaves a denominator of **306,619** documents". The exclusion appears in every logged FTS command (`AND d.volume_id NOT IN ('frus1951-54IranEd2','frus1969-76ve15p2Ed2')`). §5 discloses where it was *not* applied: "1,969 of 307,359 non-apparatus documents = 0.00641 baseline, Ed2 *retained* in the denominator — so these lifts are on a slightly different footing ... compare within each table, not across."

Compliance 24/29 = 0.83 (E3 excluded as not_applicable). Verification performed: I re-ran the memo's two appendix SQL statements against frus-copy.db and both reproduce byte-for-byte (3669|4423|1511|2097|585|779|6643 and 274|248|248|26|0), confirmed the corpus count 316839|552, the .796 volume count (88), the four subject df values (2876/1298/242/7), the whole axis-A decade table, the 694 XML files on disk, and four of the quoted document rows verbatim. This memo's numbers are real, not decorative — which is why the five failures are worth stating precisely.

Block profile: COVERAGE 2/2, IDENTITY 3/3, EXCLUSIONS 1/2 (+1 n/a), TRAPS 3/3, REPORTING 4/5, SCOPING 4/5, ARCHIVAL 4/6, P-items 3/4.

The five violations, and what each cost:
- E1: front matter and editorial notes are neither excluded nor disclosed. I measured 149 front-matter and 69 editorial-note rows inside the headline 3,669, and `is_front_matter`/`is_editorial_note` appear nowhere in report or log. §4's aside that axis A "drags in ... editorial notes" is a precision complaint, not the scoping disclosure the item asks for, and it says nothing about front matter.
- S5: Ed2 is entirely absent from both files. Three second-edition twins are in the index (377/386/418 docs) and 12 of their documents are inside axis A, so both the 3,669 and the 552-volume denominator carry an unchecked double-count.
- A2 and A6 are the substantive archival gap and they are the same gap. The memo did the source-note channel well (A1, A3, A5 all clean) but never opened a NAID-bearing resolution artifact — grep finds no `NAID`, no central-files-index.json, no collection-authority.json, no lot-claimants-index.json, no series-facts-index.json — so "M–88", "63 D 351" and "RG 59" are quoted out of source notes and stop there, which is precisely what A6 excludes. §7 discloses the footnote-channel omission honestly, but disclosure is not the behaviour the item scores.
- P3 is a near-miss on an absolute standard: the great majority of quotations carry ids that I verified, but §6(d)'s two military snippets carry none, and several §2 chapter-title quotations name no volume.

Two judgement calls I want on the record, both of which I resolved in the memo's favour and either of which a stricter marker could flip:
- A4 obeyed rests on `decimal-class-labels.json` counting as a "bundled archival-resolution artifact". It is bundled and it resolves the meaning of an archival citation (the State Department central-file class, quoted as a suffix tree and used to build the country table), but it is a labelling schedule, not one of the NAID-bearing resolution indexes. Reading A4 as requiring those would make it violated and drop ARCHIVAL to 3/6.
- R1 obeyed rests on the appendix, which reproduces exactly. But roughly fifteen queries.log entries are `<description>` placeholders and only three are expanded, so the repository profile, the lot-file ranking, the .796 suffix breakdown and the §4 extent figures have no shown SQL anywhere. The item does not say "every number", which is the only reason this is not a violation.
